quiet.title: Why this address's flood record is quiet
quiet.origin: Our counts of NWS flood reports near this address and across sampled places
quiet.text: Only 2 flood reports within 5 km of this address are in our records. We measured 25500 random places across the 51 states we have indexed: 71% had no flood report within 5 km, 12% had more than this address and 5% had the same number. A flood report exists only if someone filed one, and this is a count of reports we could place near an address. A quiet record means no report was filed close by. It does not mean nothing happened here, and it does not mean flooding is impossible.

story.totalsLine: Across these 10 events the National Weather Service recorded 7 deaths, 49 injuries and $16.1 million in recorded damage.

sentences.text: The most damaging event in the record for your zone is the High Wind of Dec 27, 2002, with recorded damage of $3,300,000 and a recorded magnitude of 45.
The National Weather Service recorded that those winds "knocked out power to around 300,000 homes" and that "Dozens of trees were downed" across western Washington.
On Dec 14, 2006, another High Wind in your zone injured 16 people, and the record puts damage at $10,000,000.
Heavy snow of 4-12 inches fell on Dec 21, 2008, and in Bellevue a tent weighted by snow collapsed at a temporary ice rink.
A Strong Wind on Jan 16, 2011 killed a state DOT worker when a tree fell on Highway 203 south of Carnation.
An Ice Storm on Jan 19, 2012 left "Downed trees" at Northwest Trek and damaged power infrastructure, with $800,000 in recorded damage.
Most recently, a High Wind on Nov 19, 2024 killed a woman when "a tree fell on her home" southeast of Kirkland.
Across King County and the zones near your address, the National Weather Service has recorded 268 weather events since 2000, including 47 High Wind and 45 Heavy Snow events.

SE-5326117.title: High Wind, Dec 27, 2002
SE-5326117.origin: NCEI Storm Events, as filed by the National Weather Service
SE-5326117.text: High Wind on Dec 27, 2002 in Seattle Metropolitan Area (forecast zone WAZ007, YOUR zone: the address is inside it). Deaths: 0. Injuries: 1. Recorded damage: $3,300,000 (about $3.3 million). Recorded magnitude: 45 (M).
SE-5326117.quote: High winds knocked out power to around 300,000 homes throughout western Washington. Dozens of trees were downed, some fell on houses and others blocked roadways. Two barges broke free from their moorings in Elliot bay, and the Tacoma Narrows bridge was closed when a trucks semi trailer was blown over. The storm also contributed to the death of a 10 year old boy, in Thurston county, who became entangled in a downed power line and was electrocuted. In downtown Seattle, a man was knocked unconscious by a flying truck canopy.

guidance.source: National Weather Service, Turn Around Don't Drown
guidance.text: Never drive around the barriers blocking a flooded road. The road may have collapsed under that water.

items.action: The Dec 14, 2006 windstorm in your area left eight people dead from carbon monoxide poisoning after improper or indoor use of barbeques or power generators. Use generators only outdoors and away from windows.

guidance.text: Use a generator, but ONLY outdoors and away from windows.
Avoid carbon monoxide poisoning. Only use generators and grills outdoors and away from windows and never heat your home with a gas stovetop or oven.

items.action: Your address has had 5 days feeling like 100°F or more since 2000, and Jun 28, 2021 felt like 114.7°F. Identify cool places such as libraries or shopping malls, and do not rely on a fan as your main cooling.

guidance.text: Identify places in your community where you can go to get cool such as libraries and shopping malls or contact your local health department to find cooling options in your area.
Do not rely on a fan as your primary cooling device. Fans create air flow and a false sense of comfort, but do not reduce body temperature or prevent heat-related illnesses.
